heuristic.applicability: Prefer when drawer/red geometry is near demonstrated support but the current TCP, joint configuration, or tracking lag differs modestly from the nominal path, including a handoff-produced entry state. It is also a local alternative when the drawer anchor estimate is less trustworthy but observed TCP/object relations are coherent.

handoff.entry_conditions: Drawer closed, partly open, or just opened; current TCP and joints are finite and reachable; object relations are coherent; gripper state is observable. Prefer modest deviation from a demonstrated approach/contact/transition rather than arbitrary recovery states.
handoff.exit_conditions: Nominal switch cue is drawer_position above 0.26 with near-zero drawer velocity, front released, and red aligned, closed upon, and observably co-moving upward with the TCP. These cues do not change task success.
handoff.failure_signatures: Repeated local commands without drawer progress, unexpected drawer motion, increasing TCP-to-front or TCP-to-red error, closed fingers without object co-motion, red drop, accumulated pose drift, IK nonconvergence or limit contact.
handoff.overlap_role: Every segment action 0:470 is supervised. Indices 230:470 duplicate the red_transfer receiving responsibility with physical actions on both sides of handle release and red pickup, totaling 2,880 overlap actions.
handoff.successor_readiness: red_transfer can accept after drawer opening and red exposure because it is trained from 230; the clean nominal handoff is red/TCP co-motion with closed fingers near 470.

heuristic.limitations: Local increments do not make long-range object displacement invariant and can accumulate drift when repeatedly applied off-distribution. A nominal increment can push after missed contact, and fresh-TCP composition cannot infer contact truth. The demonstrations do not cover alternative approach sides, blocked pulls, dropped objects, or recovery. Large TCP offsets, rotations, singular/limit-near joints and collisions remain unsafe or unreachable. drawer_frame_tracking covers reliable anchor displacement; phase_conditioned_world supplies explicit phase supervision. Any unconverged IK result is reported, not hidden.
heuristic.pipeline_implications: The caller supplies drawer calibration and intended opening only to construct relational observations; each action is decoded from the fresh measured TCP. The high-level agent should use this prior for local geometric perturbations and switch away if repeated increments do not cause expected drawer/red co-motion. drawer_frame_tracking better covers a known displaced drawer anchor; phase_conditioned_world better covers nominal geometry with uncertain stage. The standard backbone is unchanged; the prior is entirely in causal relational inputs and the Cartesian target converter.
heuristic.rationale: Observed evidence: demo1000 contains long free-space motion into the front (0-140), contact-constrained pulling (160-230), release and vertical retreat (240-300), a large reorientation/translation toward red (320-445), and initial lift by 470. Measured TCP and commanded TCP are close but not identical during motion, and final robot qpos differs across the red-Y variants (for example demo1000 versus demo1005). A predecessor or physical tracking can therefore produce a feasible TCP/joint state not exactly on the memorized path. The policy learns each target as the local SE(3) transform from that slot's measured TCP to the demonstrated commanded TCP: local translation, local rotation vector, and gripper scalar. At execution each slot is composed with the freshly measured TCP before shared IK. This preserves current robot configuration through qpos/qvel and IK while making the commanded correction local rather than an absolute world waypoint. Inputs include the drawer and red expressed relative to the current TCP, drawer progress/velocity and joint state. No action history, future state, contact truth or augmentation is used. Expected benefit, not demonstration evidence: tolerance to modest reachable TCP offsets, servo lag, and handoff arm-configuration variation.
heuristic.statement: Fresh-TCP local SE(3) increment servo for arm-entry and tracking perturbations

assignment.subgoal: Primary responsibility: acquire the drawer front, pull the drawer from closed to a reliably open state, release/retract from the drawer, and continue through the demonstrated handoff until the red block is grasped and beginning to lift. Observed contact/motion: the gripper approaches low over the drawer front, closes, pulls mainly along world -X, then opens and retreats upward before moving above and descending to the exposed red block; gripper/object co-motion is used only as an observable contact cue because contact truth is unavailable. Entry is a closed drawer (drawer_position about 0), open gripper, high TCP, red inside the drawer, and blue outside. At the nominal exit observation 470, drawer_position is 0.300, fingers are about 0.018 m, and red is grasped and lifted to z about 0.093-0.107 m while blue is unchanged. Examples: demo1000 observations 230/280 show the fully opened drawer followed by release/vertical retreat; 400/445/470 show red alignment, closure, and lift. The front images at demo1000 indices 150, 230, and 445 support the drawer-pull, open-drawer, and red-contact interpretation. Purpose/expected benefit: the retained post-opening transition should let the red-transfer successor accept a switch before or after drawer release and red contact; it is not evidence of recovery from unseen failed pulls or misgrasps.

conversion_check.description: Local transform encode/decode reconstructs demonstrated commanded TCP targets when composed with the corresponding measured pre-action TCP. Shared IK is evaluated by FK position/rotation and unchanged gripper scalar.

contract.cut_relation: Supervises every action in all assigned [0,470) segments and preserves approach, pull, release, retreat, red pickup and initial lift. The full 230:470 action overlap with red_transfer remains duplicated supervision.
contract.output_semantics: Each slot is the local SE(3) transform from that slot's measured pre-action TCP to the demonstrated commanded TCP: local translation [3] in metres, local rotation vector [3] in radians, and native gripper scalar [1]. Slots 1..8 execute t..t+7. At every physical step, the slot transform is composed on the fresh measured world TCP pose. The resulting world target is passed to panda_kinematics.solve_ik from fresh qpos; the gripper scalar is appended unchanged and interpreted by common sign semantics.
contract.parameter_semantics: drawer_origin_world_m is the world position in metres of the drawer at drawer_position=0 and drawer_orientation_wxyz is its unit wxyz calibration; both construct TCP-relative causal features. desired_open_position_m is intended scalar opening in metres, bound to 0.300 m. Learned increments are policy outputs, never caller actuator inputs.
